HANDOFF from the drafting session (2026-08-16, run from ~/git/Jobs)

State: repo has NO commits yet. Modules, templates, plan, README, .agents.yaml, project/gotchas.md, CLAUDE.md symlink and a hand-rendered AGENTS.md are all in the working tree. Make the initial commit once TYlMB (module review) is done.

Marker format, exactly as hand-rendered in AGENTS.md:
  <!-- agents:begin NAME@HASH -->
  <module body, no frontmatter>
  <!-- agents:end NAME -->
followed by one blank line. HASH = first 6 hex of SHA-256 over the module body with the LEADING frontmatter block removed. The hand render used `sed '/^---$/,/^---$/d'`, which strips ANY ---…--- block, not just a leading one — define frontmatter properly (leading block only) in the tool; the current modules have no other --- pairs so the dogfood leaf (HobdW) should still match byte-for-byte. Verify rather than assume.

Modules with `kind: file` (delegation, evidence) render to the `path:` in their frontmatter (project/agents/…), not inline. All others are inline. Default module set for `init`: core, principles, stage-build.

Registry for --all verbs: ~/.config/agents/repos, one absolute path per line.

Sources the modules were tightened from (re-read if anything seems missing): AGENTS.md in ~/git/{hirewell,timetattle,pactran,nobedan,OperativeKit,Penumbra,kura,Jobs}, plus ~/git/Jobs/project/principles.md and ~/git/hirewell/project/2026-07-27-subagent-briefing-template.md.

Design decision: file-kind modules render to their path as a whole-file single region with the same markers, so sync/diff/status use one code path. Bash sandbox blocks ~/go and network — run go commands with sandbox off per call.

internal/registry landed (TDD, 20 test cases green). API: DefaultPath() (string,error) = $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agents/repos else ~/.config/agents/repos; Read(path) ([]string,error) — missing file = empty+nil, skips blank/# lines, trims, preserves order, returns paths as written; Add(path,repo) (bool,error) — rejects non-absolute repo, filepath.Clean compare, creates parents 0755 + file 0644, idempotent and byte-identical on repeat; Remove(path,repo) (bool,error). Decisions: Add/Remove rewrite the file from its parsed lines rather than raw-append, which preserves comments/blank lines byte-for-byte and normalises a missing trailing newline; Remove does not require an absolute path so junk lines can be deleted; comparison cleans both sides.

internal/gotchas landed (TDD, 22 test cases green). API: Parse(content) Entries; Read(path) (Entries, exists bool, err error) — missing file = (nil,false,nil) so status can distinguish 'no gotchas file' from 'file with no entries'; Entries has Count()/Oldest() (time.Time,bool)/Rules() Entries; Seed(path, template []byte) (created bool, err error) — O_EXCL, never overwrites, creates project/ at 0755. Entry{Date,Headline,Body,Rule,Line}. Parsing: an entry is an H2 whose text starts with YYYY-MM-DD; preamble/undated H2s/other heading levels are body, not entries; an invalid date (2026-13-45) is skipped silently. Headline = H2 remainder trimmed of leading separators (space, em/en dash, hyphen, colon), else first **bold** span, else empty; 'rule:' prefix kept in Headline. Rule = true if EITHER the H2 remainder OR the first bold span starts with 'rule:' (case-insensitive). Decisions the brief left open: Parse returns named type Entries (assignable to []Entry both ways) so the summary helpers are methods; Body is trimmed of surrounding blank lines and carries no trailing newline; H2s inside fenced code blocks are not special-cased.

Wave 1 / agent A (internal/module + internal/manifest) — done, red/green TDD, not committed.

internal/module: Hash(body) = first 6 hex of SHA-256 (HashLength const). Parse(name, raw) splits leading-only frontmatter (kind: inline|file, path) with yaml KnownFields(true); sentinel errors ErrUnterminatedFrontmatter/ErrUnknownKind/ErrPathRequired/ErrPathNotAllowed/ErrEmptyBody. Body is left byte-for-byte except that a trailing "\n" is appended when missing; hash covers the normalised body. Load(fs.FS) reads root *.md only (no recursion), Set{Get,Names}; LoadDir(dir) wraps os.DirFS.

internal/manifest: FileName, Manifest{Modules}, Parse/Marshal/Read/Write/Resolve. yaml encoder indent 2 so output matches the checked-in .agents.yaml byte-for-byte; validation rejects missing/empty modules, duplicates, names outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$, and unknown top-level keys. Marshal and Write validate too, so an invalid manifest never reaches disk. Resolve returns *UnknownModulesError listing every unknown name.

internal/render implemented (wave 1, strict red/green TDD; 60 subtests green, gofmt/vet clean, whole repo go test green).

API: Parse(doc) -> Document{[]Segment} (SegmentText verbatim | SegmentRegion{Name,MarkerHash,Body,BeginLine,EndLine}); Document.String() round-trips byte-for-byte; Inspect(doc,mods) -> Report{Regions []RegionReport, Missing []string} with Stale/Edited/Orphan booleans, RegionReport.Fresh(), Report.AnyStale/AnyEdited/AnyOrphan; Render(doc,mods) -> string; RenderFile(existing,m) = Render with a one-element list; Diff(a,b) -> LCS line diff, 3 lines of context, '...' elision, '' when identical.

Dogfood test passes: Render(this repo's AGENTS.md, [core,principles,stage-build,go] loaded from modules/) is byte-identical and all four regions Inspect as Fresh, so the hand render and the tool agree today (test will go red if Ben's review TYlMB edits a module - that is the intended signal, not a bug in render).

Decisions worth knowing for init/sync/diff/status:
- A line that starts with '<!-- agents:begin ' / '<!-- agents:end ' but is not in canonical form is a Parse ERROR (not text), so a typo cannot silently orphan a region. Indented or mid-line marker text stays text (AGENTS.md line 40 relies on this).
- Render fills the region slots already in the doc, in document order, with the mods that have a slot, in mods order; surplus slots are deleted (dropping one immediately following blank line); mods with no slot are appended after the last region, each separated by exactly one blank line. One separator rule covers empty doc / head-only doc / append.
- Render rejects modules with a non-canonical Name or Hash, or a duplicate Name, rather than emitting a document that will not re-parse.
- Render always writes the current module body, so it overwrites hand edits. sync must call Inspect first and refuse on AnyEdited() unless --force.
- 'Needs a write' is best decided by comparing Render output to the input string, not by a flag; Inspect deliberately has no NeedsRender().
- Uses module.Hash / module.HashLength (from 1Y5td) so the hash is defined once; the marker regexps are built from HashLength. Tests recompute the hash independently.

Files: internal/render/{region,render,inspect,diff}.go + {parse,render,inspect,diff,dogfood,helpers}_test.go. Nothing outside internal/render touched.

internal/repo.Init landed (TDD). API: Init(dir, InitOptions{Modules []string (empty = DefaultModules() = core,principles,stage-build), Set module.Set, Templates fs.FS (nil skips seeding), RegistryPath string (empty skips registration)}) (InitResult, error). InitResult{Dir, Modules, ManifestWritten, Sync SyncResult, GotchasSeeded, Link LinkResult, Registered, RegistryPath}; LinkResult = LinkCreated|LinkAlready|LinkForeign. Steps: validate names (manifest.Marshal for form + manifest.Resolve for unknowns, all listed in one error) -> write .agents.yaml, or leave an existing one byte-identical when the module list matches, or *ManifestConflictError telling the user to edit it and run sync -> render through the ordinary Sync(false) path (so an existing AGENTS.md becomes the head in full and hand edits refuse) -> gotchas.Seed(project/gotchas.md) -> CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md relative symlink (a CLAUDE.md that is anything else is left alone, LinkForeign) -> registry.Add with the ABSOLUTE dir. Idempotence is tested by snapshotting every file+symlink and re-running. Decisions the brief left open: an identical-but-differently-formatted manifest is NOT reformatted; DefaultModules() is a function returning a fresh slice, not a package var; the CLI's init prints sync's refusal diffs when an existing repo has hand edits. Criteria d2d and aOo are both covered by tests (TestInitPreservesExistingAgentsFile, TestInitIdempotent) but left unticked — Ben marks them.

internal/repo.Sync landed (TDD). API: Repo.Sync(force bool) (SyncResult, error); SyncResult{Written, Fresh []string (repo-relative, target order), Edited []EditedRegion{Target, Region, Diff}}, Refused() bool; sentinel ErrHandEdited. Semantics: a target needs a write iff render.Render(current) != current, so stale markers, missing regions and orphans are one test; ANY hand-edited region anywhere aborts the whole run before a single byte is written (diff direction current->module, so '-' is what --force would throw away); nothing stale = no writes, empty result. Writes are atomic (temp file + rename in the same dir), create parent dirs at 0755, preserve an existing file's mode and use 0644 for new files, and resolve a symlinked path with filepath.EvalSymlinks first so a rename writes THROUGH a link instead of replacing it. Verified byte-for-byte no-op on a fresh repo via os.Chtimes (mtime unchanged), not just equal bytes. Criteria pa3 and c6q covered by TestSyncRefusesHandEdit and TestSyncNoOpOnFreshRepo/TestSyncRendersFileModule; left unticked.

internal/repo.Diff/Status and the four CLI verbs landed (TDD). Repo.Diff() (DiffReport{Dir, Edits []EditedRegion, Rules gotchas.Entries}, error) — module is the 'a' side so '+' lines are what the agent added (the opposite of sync's refusal diff, which shows what --force would undo); Rules are gotchas.Entries.Rules() from project/gotchas.md. Repo.Status() (Status{Dir, Modules, StaleCount, EditedCount, MissingCount, OrphanCount, GotchaCount, OldestGotcha time.Time, HasOldestGotcha, HasGotchasFile}, error) — stale and edited counted distinctly, a region that is both counts in both. CLI: persistent --modules <dir> (else the embedded modules); init --with a,b,c; sync --force; diff/status --all. Registry path is  when set, else registry.DefaultPath(), documented in the root help. --all warns on stderr and continues for a missing/unmanaged repo (diff) or prints '<path>  (missing)'/'(not managed)' (status); both exit 0. status is one tabwriter-aligned line per repo, gotchas=none when there is no gotchas file at all vs gotchas=0 for an empty one. sync prints 'AGENTS.md: core (hand-edited)' + diff to stdout and returns a sentinel error, so cobra prints the advice once on stderr and main exits 1. Criteria FnE and kmi covered by TestDiffAllWarnsAndContinues and TestStatusCounts/TestStatusCountsStaleAndEditedDistinctly; left unticked.

Dogfood evidence from the verbs wave: internal/repo/dogfood_test.go copies this repo's AGENTS.md and .agents.yaml into a temp dir, loads the EMBEDDED modules via agents.Modules(), runs repo.Init (which renders through Sync) and asserts the result is byte-identical to the hand-rendered AGENTS.md. It passes today with zero writes, so the tool reproduces the hand render exactly — the leaf itself (replacing the file in place) is still Ben's to do. If a module body changes under review the test falls back to asserting a second Sync is a no-op and logs the diff, so it will not go red on a legitimate rewrite.

data.text:
internal/source is in place; full suite green. Design record.

**Cache layout.** `<cacheDir>/sources/<sha256 hex of the URL>/` holds three things:
`git/` a bare mirror clone, `commits/<sha>/` one extracted tree per fetched
commit, and `refs/<sha256 hex of the ref>` a one-line file recording the sha a
ref resolved to at fetch time. The URL is hashed rather than sanitised so any
spelling — ssh, https, a local path — yields one flat, collision-free name; two
spellings of the same repo cost a second fetch and never a wrong answer. The
ref file is hashed because a ref may contain a slash.

**Why extract instead of checking out on demand.** The ref file plus the
extracted tree are what let `Git(name, url, ref)` load with no git process at
all: it is `os.ReadFile`, `os.Stat`, `os.DirFS`. That is the offline `check`
path, and it is proved two ways — the fixture repo is deleted and `PATH` is
pointed at an empty directory before the second load. I mutation-tested it
(added a `rev-parse` to `Git`, watched the test fail, reverted).

**Full mirror clone, not shallow.** The plan says "shallow"; I did not. Fetching
a bare local repo by sha needs `uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant`, which a
plain `git init --bare` does not set, so `--depth 1 <url> <sha>` fails against
exactly the repo the tests build and against any self-hosted source. A mirror
clone plus `git archive <sha>` works everywhere and sources are prose-sized.
Correctness over cleverness, as briefed.

**Extraction is `git archive --format=tar` into stdlib `archive/tar`.** No
dependency on a `tar` binary and no pipe between two processes. Entries are
path-checked (no absolute, no `..`) and only directories and regular files are
written — a symlink in a source could point out of the cache. Unpack goes to a
temp sibling and is renamed, so a killed fetch never leaves a half tree that a
later load would read as complete.

**The loader does NOT sandbox the user's git config.** The brief asked for
`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` on every git call
"in tests and in the loader". In the tests, yes. In the loader that would
defeat the reason the plan chose to shell out at all — "private repos work with
the user's credentials" — by disabling credential helpers, `url.insteadOf`
rewrites and SSH aliases. The loader sets only `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, so a
missing credential fails fast instead of hanging an agent with no TTY. The
tests set the hermetic vars in their own process env and the loader's children
inherit them, so nothing reads the developer's config during a test run.

**`templates/` is optional.** Git cannot track an empty directory, so a source
with no seeds cannot carry one. `modules/` missing is `ErrNoModules`; a missing
`templates/` yields an `fs.Sub` whose reads report `fs.ErrNotExist`, which is
the same outcome as an empty FS for a seed lookup by name. Only a directory
*listing* differs (error rather than empty) — flagged for whoever writes the
seed path.

**Known limitation for wave 4 (`update`).** `Resolve(url, "")` means "the
default branch" and reads the mirror's `HEAD`, which git does not update on
fetch. If a source repo later changes its default branch, an unpinned resolve
keeps the old one until the cache is dropped. `update` writes a sha, so this
only affects a repeated unpinned request. If wave 4 needs it exact, the fix is
`git ls-remote --symref <url> HEAD` in that one case.

**API.** `Source{Name, Modules fs.FS, Templates fs.FS, Commit string}`;
`FromFS(name, fsys)`; `DefaultCacheDir()`; `New(cacheDir) *Loader` with
`CacheDir()`, `Path(name, dir)`, `Git(name, url, ref)`, `Resolve(url, ref)`,
`Fetch(url, ref) (sha, error)`. Sentinels `ErrNotFetched`, `ErrUnknownRef`,
`ErrNoModules`. All primitives, no manifest type — the wiring leaf composes.

No new dependencies. `go fix`, `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go mod tidy` clean;
`go test ./...` green. Branch wt/source, not committed.

Manifest now carries sources and typed module entries (branch wt/manifest).

Shape:
- Manifest{Sources []Source, Modules []ModuleRef}. Source{Name,Git,Path,Ref} with yaml keys name/git/path/ref; ModuleRef{Source,Name}.
- ModuleRef implements yaml.Unmarshaler over the scalar entry ("name" or "source/name"); Manifest implements MarshalYAML onto a private wire struct whose Modules are strings, so the canonical file form (bare for the default source, qualified otherwise) lives in one place and KnownFields(true) still applies on decode (it propagates into nested structs — verified by a test on an unknown key inside a source).
- Parse and Marshal both fill a bare entry's Source from DefaultSource() (first listed source, else ExampleSource="example") before validating, on a cloned slice so a caller's manifest is not mutated. So a parsed ref always names its source, and Marshal drops the qualifier again when it equals the default — a hand-written "house/core" under default source house canonicalises to "core".
- Errors: ErrModuleCollision (two sources, same module name; message names both qualified), ErrUnknownSource, ErrInvalidSourceName, ErrDuplicateSource, ErrSourceLocation (both/neither of git and path; the message for a bare "example" entry says the embedded source is implicit). Same (source,name) twice stays ErrDuplicateModule.
- Resolve(m, set) kept for the single-set case; ResolveWith(m, Lookup) is the per-source checker. UnknownModulesError.Names []string became Refs []ModuleRef and the message prints qualified names.
- Helpers for the wiring leaf: ParseRef, Manifest.Ref (resolves a CLI argument against the default source and rejects an unlisted one — this is what makes "already enabled" answerable), Manifest.Entries (file form, for list/status), Manifest.SourceByName, Manifest.DefaultSource.

Not a bug: "modules: [3]" parses as a module named "3" — yaml.v3 decodes an int scalar into a string and the existing name pattern allows leading digits.

data.text:
Index region implemented on wt/index. Design decisions and why:

**The index is synthesised as a `module.Module`.** `render.Index(mods) (module.Module, bool)` builds a module named `index` — Kind inline, Body the heading + preamble + table, Hash the ordinary module hash of that body — from the enabled modules that carry `when:`, in manifest order. `repo.Targets` appends it to AGENTS.md's inline module list when it applies. Everything downstream then works untouched: Render fills or appends its region and drops it when it stops applying, Inspect marks it stale/hand-edited/orphaned, check/status/diff report it, Sync writes it, Add renders it through the ordinary sync. No verb learned about the index; the only two lines that know it exists are in Targets and in Remove.

**Remove is the one exception and needed new code.** Remove deliberately touches only the regions it was asked to, but the index body is the manifest's, so dropping a situational module would leave a row pointing at a file the same call just deleted. Added `Repo.updateIndex`, called after the region removals: it rewrites the index region in place when any `when:` module remains and deletes it when none does. It leans on a new `render.SetRegion(doc, m)` — render one named region, leave every other byte (including stale and hand-edited regions) alone — which is the primitive Render is not, and is reusable for any future single-region write.

**`index` is reserved at the module loader.** `module.ReservedName = "index"` and `module.Parse` refuses a module of that name (`ErrReservedName`), so a source can never author `modules/index.md` and collide with the generated region. Rejecting it in render instead would not work: by the time Render sees the list, the generated index is in it and indistinguishable from a source module of the same name. `index` in `.agents.yaml` was already an unknown-module error — no module of that name resolves — and there is now a test proving it.

Body is fixed: `## Situational instructions`, the one-sentence preamble, then `| Situation | File |` / `|---|---|` and one row per module, the file backticked. A `|` inside a `when:` phrase is escaped so it cannot split the row.

Design for the wiring, before writing tests.

- embed.go keeps one embedded FS (`//go:embed modules templates`); Embedded() returns
  it whole (a source root), Modules()/Templates() are fs.Sub views of the same var, so
  nothing is embedded twice and the existing callers keep working.
- repo.Open(dir, Options) replaces Open(dir, set). Options carries the source.Loader,
  the embedded FS and a FetchPolicy (FetchNever for check/status/diff/list,
  FetchMissing for sync/add/init). No module set is passed in any more: the manifest
  names the sources and Open loads them.
- Repo.Sources map[string]Sourced (Sourced = {source.Source, module.Set}) replaces
  Repo.Set; Repo.origin maps an enabled module's name to its source, which is
  unambiguous because the manifest refuses two enabled modules with one name. Seeds and
  the gotchas reseed read that source's Templates.
- Repo.Templates fs.FS is retired. The "read-only verbs create nothing" invariant it

`agents update` landed on wt/update; full suite green, `agents check` silent here. Design record.

**Shape.** `internal/repo/update.go` is the library: `(*Repo).Update(opts Options, up UpdateOptions) (UpdateResult, error)` with `UpdateOptions{Sources []string, Ref string}` and `UpdateResult{Updated []SourceUpdate, Sync SyncResult}`. `SourceUpdate{Name, From, FromCommit, To, Changes []ModuleChange}` plus `Moved() bool`. `internal/cli/update.go` is flag parsing and printing only, reusing sync's `printRefusal`, `errRefused` and `prefixed`.

**`From` vs `FromCommit`.** The manifest's ref may be a sha or a branch a human wrote. `From` is the text the manifest held; `FromCommit` is the commit that text named in the cache (empty when the cache had nothing at it). `Moved()` is `FromCommit != To`, which separates two cases the CLI prints differently: a real move (`house: 1a2b3c4 -> 5d6e7f8`, then the diffs) and Decision 7's re-pin, where only the spelling changed (`house: pinned main to 1a2b3c4`). A source whose ref already reads exactly the new sha returns nothing at all — no header, no manifest write, no render.

**Order of operations.** The old tree is loaded from the cache *before* the fetch. `Loader.Fetch(url, ref)` rewrites the cache's record of what that ref name points at, so a manifest pinned to a branch would otherwise lose the body to diff against. After every selected source is resolved, the manifest is written once (`manifest.Write`, so the file stays canonical and only `ref` values differ), then the repo is *re-opened* — the in-memory `Sources` still hold the trees of the old commits — and synced.

**Nothing moved means nothing is written.** No manifest write, no render, no seeds. A repo that is stale for some other reason is `sync`'s business; that keeps "update on a current source prints nothing and exits 0" exactly true.

**A refusal leaves the pin moved.** If a region was hand-edited, the render refuses after the manifest was rewritten. Deliberate: the pin and the diff are the decision, the render is mechanical, and the fix is `agents diff` then `agents sync --force`. Said so in DOCS.md and in the verb's help.

**Default ref: `git ls-remote --symref <url> HEAD`.** Added `source.RemoteHeadRef(url)` (a small addition to internal/source, as briefed), returning a full refname like `refs/heads/main`, with the HEAD sha as the fallback when a remote reports no symref line.

**FINDING, correcting the source leaf's note.** That note said `Resolve(url, "")` keeps resolving the mirror's stale HEAD because `git fetch` never refreshes it. On **git 2.54 that is no longer true**: a `--mirror` clone's HEAD *does* follow the remote's on fetch (verified directly — moved a bare repo's HEAD to another branch, fetched in the mirror, HEAD followed). So the end-to-end test I first wrote for this ("update follows the remote's new default branch") was green with `RemoteHeadRef` removed — it tested nothing on this machine. Per the red/green rule I deleted it and replaced it with a unit test of `RemoteHeadRef` in `internal/source/source_test.go`, mutation-checked (stub out the symref branch, the test fails). `RemoteHeadRef` still earns its place: it is correct on older gits and on any server, and it does not depend on a fetch having happened.

**Tests.** internal/repo: pin moves and the changed module is diffed and re-rendered; a commit touching only a module the repo does not enable moves the pin with no diff; an already-current source is a byte-for-byte no-op on the manifest; a hand-written branch becomes a sha; `--ref` pins a tag's commit; a path-only manifest does nothing; naming sources selects them and an unlisted name is an error naming it; a hand-edited region refuses with `ErrHandEdited` and the diff in `res.Sync`. internal/cli: header + diff + `rendered AGENTS.md` and the manifest pinned; a current source prints nothing; `--all` reports both repos, prints the refusal, exits non-zero, and still updates the clean repo. All were red first (compile failure, then unknown command).
